source_findings.finding: v2 cached optimizer group/state references became stale after load_state_dict.
source_findings.resolution: v3 repaired rebuilding; v4 independently contracts continuation. This does not explain fresh-run underperformance.

source_findings.finding: v2 output-row equalizer differs from upstream longer-axis lanes on 43x64 gate/up.
source_findings.resolution: v3 corrected lanes, without closing the fresh-return gap.

source_findings.finding: Literal upstream FP32 grad.float().lerp_ aliases and mutates its gradient input.
source_findings.resolution: v4 uses out-of-place lerp; upstream BF16 .float() makes a copy. The optimizer stack already separates input storage from p.grad; the direct ownership contract checks the arithmetic API itself.

source_findings.finding: Anvil first Gram precedes normalization; polynomial and action combine before BF16 rounding.
source_findings.resolution: v4 reuses normalized first Gram and addmm/baddbmm fusion, with BF16-rounded equalized direction. Numeric equivalence must use recorded contract errors.

source_findings.finding: FP32 model parameters serve as master weights; no BF16 mantissa reconstruction is needed.
No LM base-LR-squared slow-sign-gated decay or blindly copied transposed down-projection role multiplier.
Twin-rail phase fractions scale 1194 LM steps to actual PPO optimizer steps. Copying fractions is a hypothesis, not proof of optimal scheduling.
Final-budget diagnostic snapshot is pre-update; final model is saved after the last update.
Training frontier gain uses GAE, heldout MC gain uses lambda=1 with bootstraps; warm .85 switches from stored .95 history.
Initial BF16 ideal-spectrum errors were 14–25% on condition-number-1e4 inputs, exceeding an unsupported 12% test threshold.
source_findings.resolution: Retain distortion and FP64-accumulation sensitivity measurements; require strict FP32 oracle, well-conditioned independent BF16 rounding-boundary arithmetic, and upstream parity on the same ill-conditioned inputs. No production arithmetic was changed.

source_findings.finding: Upstream H100 wide-Gram launch requires 147456 shared bytes, exceeding this GPU's 101376-byte limit.
source_findings.resolution: Tests use unchanged upstream XXT_kernel with smaller documented tiles/stages. This checks hardware-adapted source parity; production v4 already uses native CUDA matmuls.

source_findings.finding: Report11559 lacked inherited XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and could not reach the machine-wide mlq socket.
source_findings.resolution: Final experiment/report submissions explicitly inherit XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; the training wrapper fails fast without it so autocull cannot silently lose queue access.

V4 Anvil transfers reference cascade and rail schedule fractions; v5 keeps the cascade and slow-rail engagement/blend but uses constant .85 fast EMA/lookahead. Neither copies language-model decay or role multipliers.
Culling is selective negative evidence; a cancelled run has no observed final 8M score.
Cold Anvil has no actual optimizer history in the v3 replay; warm NorMuon does.
Frontier Anvil labels contain constructor m.95, which is unused: actual replay lookahead is scheduled .93, fast beta .85, slow beta .98, blend .4385/.5615.
Three heldout rollout chunks are not independent seeds; rollout normalization updates within chunks.

validation_summary.independent_review: Read-only reviewers assessed source port and final scoring/wrapper; reporting omissions corrected.
validation_summary.final_independent_review: Passed consistency of scores, matched-step caveat, all terminal states, counts, cull evidence, frontier claims and file hashes.

conclusion.interpretation: Anvil recovers the historical NorMuon deficit and slightly exceeds Adam in the final 100-episode window on this seed, but has not established consistent or robust superiority. At the common 7.9M trailing 200k-step window, Anvil half is 8271.0 versus Adam 8308.7; early training also lags Adam.
conclusion.normuon: Momentum .85 at LR .005 reaches 8189.4 versus 5906.6 for historical longer-axis .95, a 38.65% increase. LR .0025 with .95 reaches 6932.2; higher LR .01 is culled. Faster tracking is promising evidence, not proof of a newly fixed algebra bug.
conclusion.fasttracking_v5: Constant .85 Anvil fast EMA/lookahead reaches 8171.4, 174.0 below v4 half and below it at every recorded matched step. Reject this schedule as an improvement for this configuration and seed; retain v4 as best tested.
conclusion.precision: FP32 .005 is culled at 6,237,008 steps after low 4M/6M checkpoints; no final 8M comparison is available. This negative training evidence does not support numerical idealization as a rescue.
conclusion.frontier: All 19 candidates have negative final heldout lambda=1 surrogate gain after 10 epochs. Lower rates reduce exact KL; cold Anvil is not warm Anvil, and frozen replay is not evidence of fresh-training returns. Three heldout chunks are not independent seeds.
conclusion.mechanism: Weak-mode amplification and gradient-history lag remain plausible explanations. The low-rate and momentum contrasts do not isolate a single causal mechanism; no further gross v3 NorMuon algebra bug was established.
conclusion.iteration_decision: No additional iteration warranted by this evidence. Retain best v4 BF16 LR .0025; archive failed constant-fasttracking v5. No assertion that optimizer scheduling or role rates are globally optimal.
limitations: Only HalfCheetah-v4, seed 1; no cross-seed or cross-environment robustness.
Candidate selection and culling use the same reference; marginal gains and final-window selection are not significance tests.
Historical baselines verified succeeded; shared-runtime mtime provenance supports compatibility but is not historical content-hash proof.
Terminal latest optimizer metrics occur under late learning-rate annealing; they are not late-window averages and should not replace the prior interval-level clipfraction/KL evidence.
